description: Thirty route handlers from the four corpus repositories that document access-control defects, labelled by hand from each repository's own documentation. A handler is vulnerable when the repository's tutorial, challenge list or solution notes names it as a broken-authorization or IDOR defect; it is safe when it reads or writes per-user or privileged data and the ownership or role decision is made from the authenticated identity rather than from request input. Line ranges were printed out of the pinned snapshot before being written down. No source tree is committed; benchmarks/vulnerable-corpus/README.md says how to refetch.

repositories.ground_truth: the OWASP Top 10 tutorial in artifacts/: A4 Insecure Direct Object References (allocations page) and A7 Missing Function Level Access Control (benefits admin page)
data/static/challenges.yml, category Broken Access Control: View Basket, Manipulate Basket, Forged Review, Admin Section
docs/solution/a5-broken-access-control.md: Unauthorized Access to Users API, Missing Authorization check in Edit User

cases.source: NodeGoat tutorial A4 Insecure Direct Object References: the allocations page
cases.reason: userId is read from req.params and passed straight to the DAO, so any logged-in user can read another user's allocations by changing the URL.

cases.source: NodeGoat tutorial A7 Missing Function Level Access Control: the benefits admin page
cases.reason: Lists every non-admin user's benefits and renders the page as admin for whoever is logged in; the route carries isLoggedIn only and nothing checks the caller's role.

cases.source: NodeGoat tutorial A7 Missing Function Level Access Control: the benefits admin page
cases.reason: Updates any user's benefit start date from req.body.userId with no role check; the route carries isLoggedIn only.

cases.source: not named by the NodeGoat tutorial as an access-control defect; the tutorial's note on this handler is about output encoding
cases.reason: userId comes from req.session, so the profile shown is always the caller's own.

cases.source: not named by the NodeGoat tutorial as an access-control defect; the tutorial's note on this handler is about ReDoS
cases.reason: The record updated is selected by req.session.userId, never by a client-supplied id.

cases.source: not named by the NodeGoat tutorial as an access-control defect
cases.reason: Looks up contributions by req.session.userId only.

cases.source: not named by the NodeGoat tutorial as an access-control defect; the tutorial's note on this handler is A1 server-side JS injection via eval
cases.reason: The row updated is the caller's own (req.session.userId); the eval of request fields is a different defect class and must not be counted as a missing authorization check.

cases.source: Juice Shop challenge 'View Basket' (basketAccessChallenge), category Broken Access Control
cases.reason: Loads the basket named by req.params.id and returns it without comparing it to the caller's own basket id.

cases.source: Juice Shop challenge 'Manipulate Basket' (basketManipulateChallenge), category Broken Access Control
cases.reason: The ownership check compares the first BasketId in the raw body while the item is saved with the last one, so a duplicated key puts a product into another user's basket.

cases.source: Juice Shop challenge 'Manipulate Basket' (basketManipulateChallenge), category Broken Access Control
cases.reason: Runs before PUT /api/BasketItems/:id and checks stock only; neither the item's basket nor req.body.BasketId is compared to the caller's basket.

cases.source: Juice Shop challenge 'Forged Review' (forgedReviewChallenge), category Broken Access Control
cases.reason: Updates the review selected by req.body.id without checking that its author is the authenticated user.

cases.source: Juice Shop challenge 'Forged Review' (forgedReviewChallenge), category Broken Access Control
cases.reason: Stores req.body.author as the review's author instead of the authenticated user's email, so a review can be posted in anyone's name.

cases.source: Juice Shop challenge 'Admin Section' (adminSectionChallenge), category Broken Access Control: this endpoint feeds the administration page's user table
cases.reason: Returns every user record (with masked password and TOTP secret) to any authenticated caller; the route carries isAuthorized only and nothing checks for the admin role.

cases.source: not a Juice Shop challenge; the Address routes are the repository's own example of a scoped lookup
cases.reason: The lookup is scoped by UserId, which security.appendUserId() on the route sets from the verified token, not from the client.

cases.source: not a Juice Shop challenge
cases.reason: destroy is scoped by both id and the token-derived UserId, so a caller can only delete their own address.

cases.source: not a Juice Shop challenge
cases.reason: destroy is scoped by id and the token-derived UserId.

cases.source: not a Juice Shop challenge
cases.reason: Reads the wallet for the token-derived UserId only.

cases.source: not a Juice Shop challenge
cases.reason: Resolves the caller from the bearer token and queries orders by that user's own email.

cases.source: not a Juice Shop challenge
cases.reason: Returns every order, but the route carries security.isAccounting(), which rejects any token whose role is not accounting; the role check lives on the registration line.

cases.source: not a Juice Shop challenge
cases.reason: Updates any order by id, which is the accounting role's job; security.isAccounting() on the route enforces the role.

cases.source: DVNA docs/solution/a5-broken-access-control.md, 'Unauthorized Access to Users API'
cases.reason: Returns every user record to any authenticated caller; the route carries isAuthenticated only and req.user.role is never consulted.

cases.source: DVNA docs/solution/a5-broken-access-control.md, 'Missing Authorization check in Edit User'
cases.reason: The user to update is selected by req.body.id and never compared to req.user.id, so any user's email, name and password can be changed.

cases.source: not named in DVNA docs/solution/a5-broken-access-control.md
cases.reason: Renders the form with the authenticated user's own id, email and name from req.user; nothing is read from request input.

cases.source: PyGoat Broken Access Control lab (Lab/BrokenAccess/ba.html): change the admin cookie from 0 to 1
cases.reason: The admin-only secret is released whenever the client-controlled cookie admin equals 1, before any credential is checked.

cases.source: PyGoat 2021 A1 Broken Access Control lab 1 (Lab_2021/A1_BrokenAccessControl/broken_access.html): the admin cookie
cases.reason: The admin branch is selected by request.COOKIES.get('admin') == '1', a value the client sets.

cases.source: PyGoat 2021 A1 Broken Access Control lab 2 (Lab_2021/A1_BrokenAccessControl/broken_access.html): the User-Agent header
cases.reason: The admin branch is selected by the User-Agent header equalling pygoat_admin, which any client can send.

cases.source: PyGoat 2021 A1 Broken Access Control lab 3 (Lab_2021/A1_BrokenAccessControl/broken_access.html): the secret page
cases.reason: The admin-only secret page is rendered for any authenticated user; the admin decision made in lab 3's login handler is never enforced here.

cases.source: PyGoat 2021 A1 lab 3 names the secret page, not this handler, as the defect
cases.reason: The admin flag passed to the template is decided server-side from the submitted credentials, not from a cookie or header; the hardcoded credentials are a different defect class.

cases.source: the lab index page, not named as a defect by Lab/BrokenAccess/ba.html
cases.reason: Renders a static lab description to any authenticated user; there is no per-user or privileged object to protect.

cases.source: PyGoat A10 logging lab; not an access-control lab
cases.reason: Authenticates the submitted credentials and logs the attempt; it neither reads another user's object nor grants a role from request input.
